text.p: Nigerian equities rose on Tuesday as there was a preponderance of gainers over losers, traders said.
The all-share index rose 21.22 points to 6725.27 from 6704.03 on Monday.
"The situation is relatively uncertain. Some of the usual whipping boys have turned around and there are new losers now," said James Odife of Centre-Point Investments.
Both Nigerian Breweries and Guinness, recently on the slide, advanced by 25 kobo each on Tuesday, further confirming they were back from the doldrums.
Nigerian Breweries touched 14.50 naira while Guinness closed at 6.00 naira, a 4.16 percent appreciation.
The usual gainers in oil, food and cement shares were also ahead, buoyed by sustained demand.
National Oil and Nestle were 50 kobo up at 42.00 naira and 44.20 naira, respectively, while Total at 53.00 naira gained 45 kobo.
West African Portland Cement Company climbed to 40.00 naira, going up 60 kobo. Other cement shares were unchanged.
Insurance shares picked up, courtesy of interest in AIICO and Prestige Assurance. AIICO closed 15 kobo more at 9.40 naira and Prestige rose 10 kobo to 5.00 naira.
Conglomerate Lever Brothers was the biggest loser as many investors were still dumping its shares to take profit.
Troubled airline ADC was placed on technical suspension following the grounding of its operations by the aviation ministry after its plane crashed on November 7 killing all 142 people on board.
